unresolved_questions.description: The retrieved OpenStax passage states that microtubules provide a track for vesicle movement but does not name or describe motor proteins (e.g., kinesin, dynein) or their mechanochemical cycle. The Reactome 'Kinesins' source title supports the existence of kinesin as a motor-protein class, but the retrieved passage text does not establish kinesin's role in vesicle transport. Motor-protein dependence is therefore represented as a required intermediary class but remains partially inferred from task framing.
The retrieved passages do not specify directionality (anterograde vs. retrograde) of vesicle transport along microtubules; this remains unresolved from the supplied evidence.
The retrieved passages do not restrict the microtubule-track statement for vesicles to a particular eukaryotic organism or cell type; organism scope is therefore generalized and unresolved.

The retrieved passage refers to 'vesicles' but does not define them as membrane-bounded; the 'membrane-bounded' characterization is an inference from general biological usage, not directly stated in the retrieved passage.

The stepwise ATP-dependent mechanochemical cycle of motor proteins is not described in the retrieved passages and is excluded from the model; only the causal role of a motor protein linking vesicle to microtubule is represented.
